target: live theme — Impact, templates/page.science.json, sections `hero` and `hero_banner_css`
decided_by: Malcolm: 'Our Evidence Standard' has no space between it and the banner — give it normal spacing like the other pages
note:
THE SECTION'S OWN SETTINGS WERE NOT THE FAULT. `research_standard` (text-with-icons) computes `padding-top: 0px` while its `padding-bottom` is a normal 80px, and every comparable section on the site reads 80/80 — /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research `overview`, /pages/skin-repair-renewal `content`, and this page's own `ingredients_overview`.

The cause is the `hero_banner_css` custom-html section sitting between the hero and `research_standard`. The theme's `section-spacing-collapsing` snippet emits

    #shopify-section-<id> + * { --previous-section-background-hash: <hash> }

so whatever section physically precedes another becomes its 'previous section' for the collapse test. An injected custom-html section has no background, so its hash is 0; `research_standard` has no background either, so its own hash is 0; the two match and the theme collapses the top padding — that is exactly what the collapse is designed to do between two sections that share a background.

On every other page nothing sits between the hero and the section after it, so that section's `--previous-section-background-hash` is never set, the test fails, and it keeps its 80px. Note the hero itself never emits the rule: `image-with-text-overlay` renders `section-spacing-collapsing` only `{%- unless section.settings.full_width -%}`, and this hero is full width.

FIX: move the CSS into a `liquid` block inside the hero and delete the intervening section. That restores the adjacency the theme expects — no more section between the hero and `research_standard` — so the 80px comes back on its own rather than being forced with an override.

IT ALSO FIXES A SECOND, LATENT FAULT. The old CSS was scoped by CLASS (`.shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay`), and this page carries TWO sections of that type — `hero` and `transparency`. So the hero's rules were landing on the transparency band as well; that band was only getting its own look because its `transparency_css` block scores (1,1,1) on ID against the class rule's (0,2,1). Both set `object-position: right center`, so the visible difference was limited to the text column (44vw/640px winning over 46vw/660px) and the mobile scrim (its own gradient winning over the hero's). Scoping the hero rules by `{{ section.id }}` leaves the transparency band on exactly the values it was already resolving to — verified by a full-page pixel diff at 390 and 1440.

The CSS itself is carried across unchanged, including the `min-width: 700px` guard on `object-position` — the mobile hero stays centre-cropped as it was.
